Weekly rules for the dispatchers
This section explains the steps that matter

Companion Animal Travel Desk Weekly Dispatch Rules

The Companion Animal Travel Desk keeps weekly dispatch work centered on animal safety, passenger readiness, and calm coordination across Aurelia Skyways service points. Dispatchers must review each case in plain sequence, confirm the animal care profile, and keep the record current before any travel file moves forward. The welfare coordinator reviews comfort needs and expected handling concerns, while the passenger coordinator explains the required travel steps in a clear and steady manner.

When a reservation includes a companion animal, the dispatcher must verify that all required travel details are present and consistent with the booking record. Any missing item must be referred for follow-up before the case is cleared for movement to the next stage. The dispatcher must not promise acceptance until the welfare review and the passenger briefing are both complete, because the desk depends on aligned information to avoid delay and confusion. Where animal temperament, carrier fit, feeding needs, or transfer handling requires attention, the dispatcher shall note the concern plainly and route it to the proper reviewer without embellishment.

If a passenger arrives with a changed itinerary, the dispatcher must check whether the animal arrangements still remain suitable for the revised plan. When the file shows a mismatch, the dispatcher shall pause the release of the case and seek confirmation from the relevant coordinator. Clear note keeping is required, and every update must be written so that the next agent can understand the status without searching through informal remarks. The desk must use consistent wording for ready, pending, and referred cases so that weekly reporting remains dependable.

Dispatchers are expected to maintain professional tone in all contact with travelers and internal teams. Courtesy, restraint, and careful listening are required even when the case is urgent or the passenger is uncertain. Louie, if mentioned in discussion, must be treated as a normal welfare file subject to the same review discipline as any other companion animal.

For unresolved welfare concerns, service exceptions, or a dispute about release status, contact the senior coordinator through the Companion Animal Travel Desk.
